caption: LUM-1274 — `/scoped-models` read-back: the SAME `settings.json` the LUM-1274 capture wrote (scene 9 of lum1274-scoped-models.json) is the child's HOME here, so a fresh start proves the persistence path end to end — the panel opens with the saved scope in the saved order (`2/192 enabled`, no `(unsaved)`) and `Ctrl+P` cycles only inside it. Real binary + real PTY + pyte, same harness as LUM-1286/1293/1294/1298/1308.
notes: The child runs with an explicit `--home` holding `<home>/.pi/agent/settings.json` = {"enabledModels":["ant-ling/Ling-2.6-flash","ant-ling/Ling-2.6-1T"]} — the file the previous capture's Ctrl+S produced, reorder included.
No `--model` flag: the default model is the catalog's first entry (`ant-ling/Ling-2.6-1T`), which is inside the scope, so the cycle direction is unambiguous.
`reject` on `ant-ling/Ring-2.6-1T` is the scope boundary: a full-catalog cycle reaches it after the second Ctrl+P, a scoped one wraps back inside the two saved models.
Scene 2 is `<Esc>` alone: sending `ESC` and `Ctrl+P` in one write makes crossterm read them as one chord (Alt+Ctrl+P), which is a harness lesson, not an app defect.

panels.label: 1. Alt+H then /scoped-models: the scope comes from settings.json at startup (2/192 enabled, in the saved order, not (unsaved))
2. Esc closes the panel and gives the composer back
3. Ctrl+P (app.model.cycleForward) moves to the second saved model (the scope's first entry)
4. Ctrl+P again wraps inside the saved scope instead of walking the 192-model catalog
